subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup policy should OpenClaw use when required exec-backed SecretRefs fail under a supervised gateway restart loop?
rationale: Retrying credential providers protects availability but can increase side-effecting secret-provider traffic, while degraded startup or circuit breaking changes fail-closed security semantics for required credentials.

options.title: Bounded retry, then fail fast
options.body: Add a small generic startup retry/backoff path with clear logs and keep required SecretRefs fail-closed after retries are exhausted.

options.title: Degraded startup mode
options.body: Keep the gateway online with affected credential surfaces unavailable, accepting a larger security and compatibility decision around required secrets.

options.title: External resolver guidance only
options.body: Do not change core startup behavior; document supervisor throttling and recommend batched/cached resolvers such as the linked Varlock 1Password plugin.

recommendation.title: Bounded retry, then fail fast
recommendation.body: Add a small generic startup retry/backoff path with clear logs and keep required SecretRefs fail-closed after retries are exhausted.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the SecretRef provider contract and eager runtime snapshot behavior introduced in this area.
